name: Sunwoda (Sunwoda Electronic / Sunwoda Energy)
headquarters: Shenzhen, Guangdong, China (storage arm: Sunwoda Energy Technology, Guangming District, Shenzhen)

ownership.notes: Family-controlled — co-founders Wang Mingwang and Wang Wei are named controlling shareholders and actual controllers. Swiss GDRs on SIX since 2022; Hong Kong H-share IPO refiled Jan 30, 2026 (Goldman Sachs + CITIC co-sponsors), not yet listed.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Sunwoda is the fastest-growing member of the Chinese storage top ten — a consumer-battery giant (world #1 in phone battery shipments) that built a two-hat storage business: a top-10 merchant storage-cell supplier that was first to mass-produce a 600+ Ah-class cell (684 Ah, one million units in under three months), and a ~#9 global system integrator (Benchmark, ~4% share) fielding its own NoahX containers at 25.6 GWh of 2025 system volume (+188% YoY, company-claimed). The catch is that the growth sits on a barely profitable base — core (ex-non-recurring) profit was roughly zero in Q1 2026, EV/storage-cell gross margin is under 5%, and a RMB 2.31B cell-quality lawsuit from VREMT was settled at an estimated RMB 0.5-0.8B profit hit. In the US it has no grid-scale project record, no UL 9540 system listing surfaced, and full FEOC/tariff exposure — its US relevance runs through the AIDC backup/BBU niche (72 Ah 8C cells, 800 V rack systems), not containerized BESS.
ecosystemRole: We assess Sunwoda as a peer-tier Chinese competitor that will contest Hithium in Europe, Australia, and Asia-Pacific grid tenders and in the AIDC backup lane, but not in US containerized BESS: as a Chinese-controlled prohibited foreign entity with no US manufacturing, no US reference projects, and cells booked against a sub-5% margin price war, it lacks both the compliance path and the local footprint to bid US ITC-linked projects. Its more strategic role in the web is upstream and sideways — it supplies cells to other integrators (Sungrow awarded it a Global Strategic Partner award; Tesla added it as a fifth EV cell supplier in April 2026), so Sunwoda content can appear inside competitors' systems, and its four-tier AIDC energy architecture (grid-side storage → campus backup → rack backup → BBU) mirrors the pitch Hithium would need to make to data-center accounts.

productsAndServices.name: NoahX utility-scale containerized BESS platform
productsAndServices.description: Current-generation liquid-cooled 20-ft LFP containers on the 625 Ah cell: NoahX-1500/2752 (2,752 kWh), NoahX-1500/4170 (4,170 kWh), and NoahX-1500/6528-L1 (6,528 kWh). Utility range spans 344 kWh to 6.88 MWh — the top end pairs with the new 684 Ah cell (company: a 20-ft container with 684 Ah delivers '6.9 MWh or higher'). Prior generation NoahX 2.0 (RE+ 2023) was a 4.17/5 MWh 20-ft block on 314 Ah cells.
productsAndServices.positioning: Volume challenger in the 5-6.5 MWh 20-ft class — competitive on cell vertical integration and price rather than bankability track record.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to developers/utilities and via distribution/framework partners (IBC SOLAR and BayWa r.e. in Germany/Europe, City Electrical Factors in UK/Ireland); project-investment push via a RMB 500M standalone-storage fund (Jul 2026).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Grid-side independent storage (China), utility BESS (Europe, Australia, South/Southeast Asia, Middle East), distribution-grid parks (Belgium references).
productsAndServices.roadmap: 684 Ah container top end scaling; downstream project ownership via the Tianjin Kaixin storage fund (≥70% into standalone storage projects).

productsAndServices.name: Merchant energy-storage cells (684/588/314/280 Ah + high-rate line)
productsAndServices.description: Top-10 global storage-cell supplier (InfoLink H1 2025 — first entry into that top ten). 684 Ah stacked LFP (>440 Wh/L, >20-yr life, thermal-electric separation) debuted at RE+ 25 (Sep 2025), mass production from Oct 2025, one-millionth cell Dec 29, 2025; company claims 27% fewer containers and ~8% LCOE reduction versus 314 Ah builds. Legacy 280/314 Ah 0.5C lines (8,000/12,000 cycles); high-rate line: 72 Ah 8C (data-center backup) and 100 Ah 1C.
productsAndServices.positioning: Early mover in actual 600+ Ah-class volume — ahead of much of the field's 587/625/688 Ah roadmaps in produced units, though from a much smaller base than CATL/EVE/Hithium.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Merchant supply to system integrators (Sungrow relationship evidenced by its Global Strategic Partner Award 2025; a 1.6 GWh cell-supply agreement with an undisclosed integrator signed Nov 2025, first shipments Q1 2026) alongside internal NoahX consumption.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: System integrators and OEMs globally; storage cells are booked inside the 'EV battery' reporting segment.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 684 Ah targeted at >30% of storage volume (SMM via ess-news); 2026 global cell market forecast 1,090 GWh (+70%, ICC) with AIDC storage demand named as a driver.

productsAndServices.name: AIDC / network-energy backup power (BBU, UPS, HVDC)
productsAndServices.description: Dedicated data-center backup line in the Network Energy division: UPS/HVDC backup from 1 kVA to 800 kVA; rack cabinets 480140 (max 300 kW short-duration) and 480100 (50 kW long-duration); high-rate cells (72 Ah 8C; 5C pulse-charge/10C discharge systems); voltage platforms 320-576 V with 800 V-architecture 6C/10C systems launching; claimed max single-cabinet power density 760 kW. Deployed references include Shanghai data-center HVDC backup (512V50Ah); pilots with 'leading cloud service providers' claimed since 2016.
productsAndServices.positioning: Four-tier AIDC energy architecture marketed: grid-side large storage → campus hourly backup → rack minute-level backup → BBU millisecond backup. This is Sunwoda's most credible US-relevant lane — UPS/backup sales don't claim ITC and are less FEOC-constrained than grid BESS.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and via cloud/colocation procurement; showcased at Data Centre World London (Mar 2026) and Data Center World America, Washington DC (Apr 2026).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI data centers, cloud service providers, telecom.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 2025 annual report names AIDC as a strategic growth vector for both storage cells (US AIDC construction demand) and network energy, with an in-development high-rate storage system R&D program for AIDC load-fluctuation scenarios.

productsAndServices.name: C&I, residential, and mobile ESS
productsAndServices.description: OASIS family (215/232/261 kWh all-in-one; 344/372 kWh liquid-cooled cabinets), 179 kWh outdoor cabinet (2025), Atrix/SunESS residential (5-60 kWh; SunESS H launched Jun 2026), and a 2 MWh 10-m mobile ESS vehicle ('Xin Ji Yuan 2000', 2025).
productsAndServices.positioning: Breadth play across segments; C&I/resi volume flows through the same European distribution partnerships.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Distribution (CEF UK/Ireland; IBC SOLAR; BayWa r.e.) and direct.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Not disclosed beyond continued European channel expansion.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Sunwoda's two-hat model — top-10 merchant cell supplier AND ~#9 system integrator — as both its edge and its structural conflict: it sells cells to integrators it competes with downstream (Sungrow gave it a strategic-partner award while fielding rival containers), which caps how far partners will let it climb the integration stack.

(High confidence) We assess the US containerized-BESS market as effectively closed to Sunwoda near-term: Chinese-controlled FEOC status, the 25% Section 301 step-up (Jan 2026), no US project record, no US manufacturing or announced plan, and no UL 9540 full-system listing surfaced. Its US play is the AIDC backup/BBU niche, which doesn't claim ITC — the same asymmetry Hithium faces, minus Hithium's NDAA §154 naming.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the 684 Ah early-mover position as real but perishable — one million cells in under three months is genuine volume leadership in the 600+ Ah class, but CATL/EVE/Hithium roadmaps close the gap through 2026-2027, and Sunwoda's ranking depends on which aggregator counts (Benchmark top-10 yes; InfoLink top-tier no).

(High confidence) We assess the financial base as the key fragility: core ex-NRI profit near zero (Q1 2026), EV/storage-cell gross margin under 5%, OCF down 95%, long-term borrowings up 51% in a quarter, and heavy Thailand/Vietnam capex — the storage expansion is being funded from a barely profitable core amid the Chinese price war, making the HK IPO execution-critical.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: Sunwoda is the closest structural analogue to Hithium among the nine Batch A competitors — a cell-first Chinese player pushing into integration with a big-cell flagship and an AIDC backup line — so its channel choices (European distribution, Australia anchor deals, US backup-only posture) are a live preview of the moves available to Hithium, and the two will bid against each other most often in Europe, Australia, and AIDC backup RFPs.

As a Chinese-controlled prohibited foreign entity with no US manufacturing it can't bid US ITC-linked projects, so the contests land in European distribution, Australian anchor deals, and the US AIDC backup/BBU niche that doesn't claim ITC.
